auditor: Real Estate Board of New York
title: New York City Last-Mile Facility Special Permit Study
plain_title: Study of a proposed permit for package delivery warehouses
agency: New York City Department of City Planning
what_they_audited: A study by HR&A Advisors, with traffic and emissions analysis by AKRF, prepared for the Real Estate Board of New York on what a proposed special permit for last-mile package delivery facilities would mean for New York City. It looks at market trends, the effect of last-mile growth so far, the likely impact of the permit and whether other policies would work better.
background: The Department of City Planning is studying a special permit for last-mile distribution facilities following commitments the Adams administration made to the City Council, and released a draft scope of work for environmental review in March 2025. Under that draft the permit would apply to new parcel delivery facilities in manufacturing, mixed-use and C8 districts, with exemptions including facilities under 50,000 square feet and water-dependent facilities.

recommendations: Continue the city's existing efforts to move freight in greener ways, including microhubs, electric cargo bikes, package lockers and the Blue Highways program that uses the city's waterways.

Keep incentivizing electric truck fleets and devote more resources to those programs, including expanding the city's Clean Trucks Program beyond businesses in industrial business zones to all New York City businesses that run truck fleets.
Improve enforcement of quality of life violations so that last-mile operators face consequences that actually change how they behave in the neighborhoods around their facilities.
